text: Walter Vinson Grant Jr., born on May 25, 1945, is an American televangelist whose ministry has been based in the Greater Dallas area. He began his career in Cincinnati, Ohio, in the mid-1970s with the "Cathedral of Compassion" in the Over-the-Rhine area before moving to the suburbs of St. Bernard until the early 1980s. In 1983, he took over Soul's Harbor Church in the Oak Cliff section of Dallas and expanded its ministry, later renaming it "Eagles Nest Cathedral." In 1987, he purchased 28 acres (11 hectares) in the southwest section of Dallas, near Dallas Baptist University, and built the "Eagle's Nest Family Church," which had a 5000-seat capacity, pastoring it until 1996. Grant was convicted in 1996 of tax evasion for failing to report $375,000 in taxable income, including $100,000 from church members used as a down payment on a $1.2 million home in Desoto, Texas, which he admitted to in an undercover video. Judge Joe Kendall sentenced him to 16 months in prison, a $30,000 fine (to be paid after release), and an additional year of probation, along with 100 hours of community service, publication of his arrest and sentence to his mailing list, and ongoing financial reporting to the court. He was released on September 18, 1997, and restarted his ministry under the name Eagles Nest Cathedral. His wife, Brenda Gayle Hayes, died on October 6, 2020. He has three adult children: daughter Misty and stepsons Barry and Mark Anderson. After attending Southwestern Assemblies of God Bible University, he earned undergraduate degrees in English Literature and Religion and a Master's Degree in History from Dallas Baptist University. He holds two honorary degrees from Kingsway Bible University (Des Moines, Iowa) and the Colonial Academy (Chicago). Paranormal investigator James Randi criticized Grant in his 1987 book, The Faith Healers, stating that Grant's claimed degree from "Midstates Bible College" in Des Moines was fraudulent, as the institution was not accredited, registered, or listed in public records. Grant claimed he had an "honorary D.D. degree" from Mid-States Bible College, which later became Kingsway Christian College, based on a formula involving books written, years in ministry, and media appearances. Grant denied being a faith healer, stating that any healing is a gift from God and he is merely a "mortal conduit." In 1986–87, Randi reported that Grant used audience members pre-placed in wheelchairs and a "sleight of hand" trick to make a leg appear to grow, with information gathered by Grant's wife via slips of paper in a Bible. In 1987, Bruce Buursma of the Chicago Tribune reported that Andrew A. Skolnick was "healed" by Grant and Peter Popoff. In 1991, ABC News and the Trinity Foundation investigated Grant during a Primetime Live exposé on Robert Tilton, with the Dallas Observer later claiming the report used deceptive techniques and that a key element was "bogus." The Trinity Foundation also published a photo of a naked Grant from his trash in their satirical magazine, The Door. In 1996, the Dallas Morning News reported that one of Grant's fundraising letters was written by Gene Ewing, a marketing executive. In 2003, WAGA-TV found that Grant arrived early at revivals and pre-selected audience members to "heal," with two of three claimed healings resulting in worse conditions and one assisting with setup. The "healing the short leg" was exposed as a magic trick by James Randi. In 2006, WWBT-TV aired an investigation on Grant during a faith healing service in Richmond. In 2010, Free Inquiry noted that Grant's practices had not changed significantly over twenty years. In 2011, British mentalist Derren Brown aired a program, "Miracles for Sale," on Channel 4, where Grant falsely claimed to know a member's name from a contact card and performed a leg-lengthening trick using the same shoe-manipulation technique Brown had previously exposed. Following his conviction, Grant transferred the Eagles Nest Cathedral facility to T. D. Jakes, who renamed it "The Potter's House." Originally located in Pleasant Grove, the church moved in August 2012 to a historic downtown Dallas property at 1508 Cadiz Street, the former home of the First Church of Christ, Scientist, where it now holds almost nightly services from 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM. Grant's wife was indicted on charges of blocking the IRS and evading taxes; she initially pleaded guilty but withdrew the plea and was later acquitted.
